title: Phylogenetically-Mixed Agent Architectures
content: One way to construct embodied computational agents for a variety of tasks is to assemble different modules optimized for different functions. Yet merely designing this utilizing a top-down approach does not capture how the agent produces a morphology that has been evaluated with respect to behavioral states and interactions with the environment. The approach introduced here is to evolve a variety of components with a relational history (phylogeny) while combining the best candidates into a modular system. Agentic coding techniques are used to build a pipeline implementing a process of diversification, selection, and composition. Our computational pipeline includes reservoir networks, forward/reverse diffusion processes, generative adversarial models, evolutionary computation, and hypergraph representations. A variety of morphologies are generated and evaluated in terms of our selection criteria. The resulting evolutionary lineages are assembled into a hypergraph identifying nested or categorical relationships. As an initial demonstration, we utilize a toy synthetic dataset of simple shapes and a dataset based on Braitenberg’s Vehicles (BVs). Phylogenetic mixing relies on variety to select the most viable forms and produce the composition of architectures. A generalist architecture should be able to perform a wide variety of tasks with the ability to connect between domains.
